anomalies.observed: R6 (10k) is connected between +3V3 and FLOAT_HIGH, while R9 (10k) is connected between FLOAT_LOW and GND.
anomalies.expected: The specification states R6 should pull FLOAT_LOW to +3V3 and R9 should pull FLOAT_HIGH to GND.

evidence.quote: Sheet 1, Water Level Sensor/Switches: R6 10k from +3V3 to FLOAT_HIGH; R9 10k from FLOAT_LOW to GND

anomalies.impact: The default/inactive states of the float-switch inputs are inverted, which can defeat the intended low-water pump cutoff and high-water ATO overflow interlock.

anomalies.observed: The EN pins of all three TMC2209 drivers are tied only to the global label STEP_PDIS. No other STEP_PDIS source or connection appears on the MCU/SoC sheet.
anomalies.expected: The TMC2209 EN input is active-low and must be driven low, tied to GND, or connected to a real GPIO; a floating enable net is not a valid enable state.

evidence.quote: Sheet 2, Peristaltic Pump Drivers: U5/U6/U7 pin 2 EN tied to global label STEP_PDIS
Three TMC2209 stepper-motor driver ICs (U5, U6, U7) ... firmware drives these pumps as plain GPIO on/off switches

anomalies.impact: With the TMC2209 enable pins floating, the three peristaltic pump drivers may remain disabled or undefined, so the dosing pumps will not run as intended.

parsed.summary: The drawing shows two likely deviations from the intended design: the float-switch pull resistors R6/R9 are swapped relative to the specified nets, and the TMC2209 EN pins are tied only to an otherwise unconnected STEP_PDIS net, which can leave all three dosing-pump drivers disabled.
